caption: A waiting room modelled on the Baths of Caracalla, built by a railway company and open to anyone holding a ticket.
pairing_note: The strongest control available: same city, same site, same railway, same purpose, and only the design changed. The 1910 station was demolished in 1963; the replacement concourse opened beneath Madison Square Garden in 1968.

caption: Vincent Scully on the replacement: one entered the city like a god; one scuttles in now like a rat.
Modernist in every structural sense, and warm with it: hand-made brick, timber, and a grass courtyard raised above the street.
pairing_note: Both are postwar modernist civic buildings by celebrated architects, sixteen years apart. This pair is here to argue against our own side: the problem is not modernism. Aalto's building is as modern as Boston's, and people are fond of it.

caption: Garlanded by critics on completion, and voted among the most disliked buildings in America repeatedly since.
Municipal housing for dock workers, in sculpted brick, with its own post office and meeting hall. Still lived in a century later.
pairing_note: Both were avant-garde municipal housing schemes by architects at the top of their profession, built as showpieces of what social housing could be. One is protected and well loved by the people in it; the other was demolished while critics campaigned to save it.

caption: Streets in the sky for more than two hundred families. Demolition began in 2017, over the objections of architects rather than residents.
Completed in 2007, drawing on Mughal, Moorish and Ottoman precedent. Proof that a living tradition can still build at the highest level.
pairing_note: Both are major modern religious buildings by leading designers with national backing. Liverpool has real defenders and its interior light is genuinely admired; it is here because its fabric failed within a few years, which is a cost that arguments about beauty are usually accused of ignoring.

caption: Built fast and cheaply after Lutyens's vast design was abandoned; leaking within a few years, and the subject of later legal action over the defects.
A glass and steel dome entered through the Tsuzumi-mon, a timber gate shaped after the hand drum used in Noh theatre.
pairing_note: Two large stations inserted into historic Japanese cities within a decade of each other, both thoroughly modern, both generously funded. Kanazawa carries its city's tradition into new material; Kyoto was controversial before it opened and remains so.

caption: Some four hundred and seventy metres of steel and glass in Japan's historic capital, built over objections that it would overwhelm the city it serves.
Several thousand homes begun in 1997 in a traditional Dutch idiom, sold at ordinary market prices.
pairing_note: Two large planned residential districts in the same country, both state-backed, both intended as models of their moment. They are roughly thirty years apart, which makes this the weakest control in the set; the note is here to say so rather than hide it.

caption: Some thirteen thousand homes in hexagonal slab blocks, separated by design from traffic, shops and street life. Large parts were demolished from the 1990s.
